claims.claim: Arm remains a foundational compute architecture/IP layer spanning mobile, edge and data center; FY2026 royalty revenue rose 21% and management attributes growth to higher-royalty Armv9 technology, while data-center royalty more than doubled year over year in Q4.

The causal path is broad but not monopoly-like: customer silicon adoption and product lifecycles mediate royalties, while Arm's move into AGI production silicon adds a new execution path that had no material FY2026 revenue contribution yet.
Arm's structural resilience benefits from a large developer ecosystem and diversified end markets, but customer and end-market concentration remain material counterweights.

falsifiers: Sustained growth in compute units with declining Arm royalty economics would weaken pricing/bottleneck control.
Material architecture substitution at major mobile/data-center customers would weaken ecosystem resilience.
AGI silicon investment without commercially material adoption would weaken the production-silicon expansion thesis.

risks.risk: Customer concentration can transmit a few customers' strategic changes directly into Arm economics.
Architecture substitution and customer in-house design choices remain credible long-run pressure points.

unknowns.unknown: AGI CPU has not yet demonstrated material revenue contribution in the cited FY2026 period.

claims.claim: The strongest present challenge is concentration and related-party dependence, not an invented accounting defect: Arm's top five customers including Arm China and SoftBank represented about 57% of FY2026 revenue, with Arm China alone about 16%.
Mobile application processors still represented about 43% of FY2026 royalty revenue, so the AI/data-center diversification thesis is progressing but has not eliminated mobile-cycle dependence.
FY2026 related-party revenue increased sharply, making source-level separation of external-customer growth from related-party growth important for confidence calibration.

risks.risk: Top-five customer concentration is 57% of FY2026 revenue.
SoftBank/affiliate arrangements create related-party dependence requiring conservative interpretation.

contradictions.contradiction: Broad AI-platform narrative coexists with still-material mobile royalty concentration and high customer concentration.
contradictions.resolution: Treat diversification as strengthening but incomplete, not as a present contradiction requiring blockage.

unknowns.unknown: No evidence in this Beta object establishes a present governance abuse or accounting-quality defect.
